notes: Run this benchmark from a repository with GitHub Actions checks and a safe disposable branch.
Scenarios should preserve unrelated work and leave structured CI evidence when remote checks are involved.
Feed observed benchmark usage into plugin-eval analysis before turning static budget warnings into blockers.
setupQuestions: Which repository and branch should represent the daily-driver delivery workflow?
Which PR or workflow run can be used safely for live CI evidence?
Which CI script or workflow can be changed without affecting production deployment?
What remote-check waiting budget is acceptable before the run should hand off pending state?

scenarios.title: Configured issue backend dependency evidence
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether Effective Delivery selects the configured issue host, uses the native provider CLI, and keeps direct blocker evidence distinct from hierarchy and transitive claims.
scenarios.userInput: Use Effective Delivery to inspect item 42 through the configured issue backend and report its direct blockers. If Jira is selected, use Atlassian acli. Do not create, edit, comment on, link, transition, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run resolves GITHUB or JIRA before provider execution and inspects capability support.
GitHub reads use gh and Jira reads use acli jira workitem commands.
Each BLOCKS edge preserves source-to-target direction from native relationship data.
The result declares depth one and does not claim hierarchy or transitive completeness.

scenarios.title: CI triage from current run evidence
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether CI failure work starts from live GitHub check/run evidence and fixes the owning source rather than guessing from stale local state.
scenarios.userInput: Use Effective Delivery to triage a failing GitHub Actions check. Identify the current failing job and run URL, prepare the owning source or workflow repair locally, and run the closest local proof. Do not push, rerun, dispatch, comment on, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run cites current PR metadata from the GitHub app when available, uses native gh only for a connector gap and Actions evidence, and pins the evidence to the head SHA.
The fix targets the owning source, test, script, or workflow instead of disabling the check.
The final evidence includes local validation and the current remote check state without changing it.

scenarios.title: Event-driven structured green claim
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether PR readiness claims use structured current-head evidence, await meaningful events without model-driven polling, and refuse to collapse pending or unknown states into green.
scenarios.userInput: Use Effective Delivery to tell me whether PR 42 is green. Use the connected GitHub app first for supported PR metadata, native gh only for a connector gap, and the native gh-backed observer for CI state. If checks are pending, arm one required-check status-change event with an automatic duration-informed timeout, yield instead of polling, and process only the event that resumes you. Do not push, rerun, dispatch, comment on, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Supported PR metadata comes from the connected GitHub app when available; native gh fills only a connector gap, and the observer classifies the current head.
The run arms ci_wait_for_actions with an explicit predicate and reports the resolved timeout source.
The model invokes one bounded await instead of unchanged status checks; a still-pending event is processed once and re-armed.
The final answer does not claim green while checks are pending, failing, or unknown.

scenarios.title: Composable workflow authoring
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether workflow authoring favors reusable scripts, least-privilege permissions, concurrency, and local proof.
scenarios.userInput: Use Effective Delivery to revise a GitHub Actions workflow so repeated setup or validation logic becomes reusable and the jobs keep explicit permissions, concurrency, and local validation commands. Do not commit, push, dispatch, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Shared logic is moved to workflow_call or a versioned repo script when reuse is needed.
Workflow permissions and concurrency are explicit and narrow.
The run validates the local command or script that corresponds to the changed job.

scenarios.title: Workflow graph optimization preserves proof
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether CI optimization removes false dependencies and repeated setup while preserving proof outputs and using deterministic median-timed graph evidence.
scenarios.userInput: Use Effective Delivery to optimize this workflow's dependency graph. Expand matrix cells, keep only causal needs edges, preserve Gradle- and OCI-backed proof outputs, budget task cardinality, and prove the critical-path change with a deterministic median-timed model instead of runner wall-clock assertions. Do not commit, push, dispatch, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run models each matrix cell or reusable invocation as an execution node and removes dependencies on unrelated required jobs.
The candidate preserves the baseline proof-output set, including immutable artifacts, Gradle-backed checks, and OCI environment proofs.
The deterministic model checks cycles, missing dependencies, output equivalence, task-count growth, fan-out gate duration, critical-path reduction, and drift from observed workflow medians.
Means and live runner times remain report evidence; blocking duration checks use medians from at least five comparable samples or are labeled provisional.

scenarios.title: PR green loop composes Git and CI
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether branch, commit, push, PR, and event-driven CI observation remain one composed delivery workflow without losing scoped staging or check evidence.
scenarios.userInput: Use Effective Delivery with Git Operations to prepare a focused local change, audit scoped staging, and produce a PR and CI handoff plan. Do not commit, push, open or update a PR, arm remote events, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run preserves unrelated work and stages only the requested change set.
The proposed PR handoff includes branch, base, prospective validation commands, and residual risks.
Any remote check facts are read-only, current-head observations and are not changed by the run.
